coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Ministry of Agriculture keeps a beekeeper registry: 198 apiaries, 1,270+ colonies, 137 active of 520 on the books (Aug 2025, https://barbadostoday.bb/2025/08/31/govt-steps-up-support-for-budding-beekeepers-amid-hurdles/). Only 2-3 commercial producers; 95% of honey is imported (https://barbadostoday.bb/2026/05/20/beekeeping-biz-a-buzz-as-honey-imports-dominate/). No registration duty, labelling rule or fee found. Pool too small; not a candidate.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Underground Water Control Act Cap. 283 was repealed by the Barbados Water Authority (Amendment) Act 2023 (bill text https://governmentprintery.gov.bb/?p=2991, Gazette 23 Oct 2023; enactment/commencement not confirmed). New s.18B-18J: licence needed to sink, deepen, alter, reuse or abstract from any well/borehole; licences valid 1 year, non-transferable, renewal applied at least 1 month before expiry; existing Cap. 283 licences lapse 12 months after commencement; fines up to BBD 25,000 and 5 years; Water and Wells Management Committee advises the Minister. Government is also building a record of well locations (https://www.cbc.bb/news/local-news/government-to-establish-record-of-well-locations/). See candidate on well-licence tracking.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Nation News (https://nationnews.com/?p=94733, undated, budget-era) reports private waste haulers must register and be licensed by the Sanitation Service Authority, pay an annual licence fee and hold an annual Barbados Revenue Authority tax clearance certificate. No septage-specific licence found; current status unverified. Small pool.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Safety and Health at Work Act Cap. 356 ss.29-31 (formerly Factories Act) requires examination of air receivers, steam receivers and steam boilers by Government-appointed competent persons; Labour Department publishes the list, updated June 2026 (https://labour.gov.bb/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/List-of-Competent-persons-for-the-Examination-of-Air-Receivers-Steam-Receivers-and-Steam-Boilers-as-at-2026.pdf, PDF unreadable by fetch). coverage.category: 38. Money laundering and depositor protection Acts 2026 (Acts 2026-20, 2026-24)
coverage.found: Protection of Depositors Bill 2026: tabled and passed by the House 23-24 June 2026; repeals Deposit Insurance Act and extends BDIC cover (BBD 25,000 per depositor) to credit unions for the first time; Gazette 25 Jun 2026 (https://www.barbadosparliament.com/uploads/gazette/Gazette_June_25_2026_Part_A_CLXI_No_74_with_Bill.pdf, PDF binary, unreadable by fetch). The contents list shows initial contribution, annual premium, filing of deposit liabilities, accounts/audit and year-end reports, but not the wording, rates or deadlines; Senate passage and commencement not confirmed. Could not find any text or news for a 2026 Money Laundering amendment (Act 2026-24); no source confirms its dealer/DNFBP provisions. Context: Compliance Unit of the Anti-Money Laundering Authority (Attorney General's Office) registers and supervises DNFBPs (accountants, attorneys, precious metals/stones dealers, real estate agents, TCSPs); a sub-working group is drafting a local DNFBP regime and per-sector AML guidelines; next CFATF mutual-evaluation on-site is June 2027 (https://barbadostoday.bb/2026/05/13/countdown-on-one-year-to-prove-compliance-with-global-regulators/). The Act 2026-24 text remains unread.

result.competitor: Free BTPA online first-time application portal (barbadostouristaccommodation.com) handles registration. No Barbados-specific compliance software found; I didn't confirm whether property managers offer registration help (search returned none). Online platforms handle levy collection (K04). result.duty: Not in force (checked 2026-10-09). Tourist Accommodation Bill, 2025: gazetted 7 Aug 2025, passed House 16 Sep 2025 with no amendments, parliament archive lists current stage as The Senate; per Parliament messages page it was referred to a joint select committee on economic and productive sectors on 3 Dec 2025. Barbados Today editorial (26 Sep 2025) reports govt paused it. I found no Senate passage, assent or commencement date. Claim cites nationnews ?p=372005 as reporting House passage in 2026, but the page returned 403 and I couldn't verify it. A search summary describes a Nation page dated 29 Apr 2026 (?p=371832) as reporting the bill introduced 'recently', but it also returned 403; its content could not be checked. Proposed provisions (not law): licence/classify/inspect all accommodation, 2-year licence, fines up to BBD 250,000, 5 years for existing operators. Existing duty in force: villas for reward must register with the BTPA (older Act per search snippets); the BTPA runs an annual licensing cycle (2024 press release) and sends monthly lists to the Revenue Commissioner. Tourism Levy (Amendment) bill (as amended 14 Jan 2026) requires providers and marketplace facilitators to register with the Authority. Levies are a separate duty (K04).
result.market: Ministry of Tourism: 1,401 registered short-term visitor accommodations, with 1,201 described as unregulated (tourism.gov.bb press release, date unconfirmed). Industry group warned the bill could close over 6,500 small and micro short-term rental operators (Barbados Today, Sep 2025). A few thousand units at most; small market.
result.reason: The new duty the claim relies on is not in force. Parliament's record shows the Tourist Accommodation Bill, 2025 passed the House on 16 Sep 2025 without amendments, and its current stage is "The Senate". A Parliament message says it went to a joint select committee on 3 Dec 2025. Barbados Today reported a government pause. I found no Senate vote, assent or commencement date. The claim says the Nation reported House passage in 2026, but that page returned 403, so I couldn't confirm what it says. BTPA registration of villas is already required under an existing law, through a free online portal. The one-off filing and simple licence give little reason to pay for software, and the market is small: the ministry counts 1,401 registered units, and industry says about 6,500 operators.

The Act exists: Act 2026-12 passed the Senate on 10 June and the House on 16 June, and was gazetted 22 June 2026. Its commencement is by proclamation, and I found no proclamation, so I can't confirm the duty is in force. The Part III pharmacy premises provisions were seen only as section headings; I did not verify the six-week deadline, three-year renewal or penalties. I did not search for competitors or a state portal and found no pharmacy count. The buyer pool is probably small (a few hundred at most), and the duty is mostly a one-off registration followed by a three-year renewal. That gives low frequency, a small market and an unknown regulator portal, so the score stays at 3.

The duty is real. The Compliance Unit (Office of the Attorney General, launched Nov 2022) supervises DNFBPs under the Second Schedule of the MLFT Act: accountants, attorneys, precious-metal dealers and real estate agents. It registers them, and complianceunit.gov.bb offers questionnaires, STR filing and sanctions lists. I could not confirm a periodic return, fee, penalty, firm count, or the content of Act 2026-24; my search found no text of it. The complianceunit.gov.bb fetch returned 503. A mutual-evaluation review team visits in June 2027, which may drive urgency. The state portal already covers part of the job, and the market is probably only hundreds of firms in a small country. No Barbados-specific competitor was found, but I did not search for one thoroughly. Pain and willingness to pay are unproven.

The Act exists: the Barbados Water Authority (Amendment) Act 2023 (Cap. 274A) covers well management, and ECOLEX lists it as repealing the old Underground Water Control Act. I found no proclamation or commencement date, so I can't confirm the annual licence regime is in force. I found no enforcement news, no wells-licensing portal and no competing software, but the searches were thin. The BWA "Where are the Wells" campaign (Mar 2023) shows it is building a register of licensed abstractors, which suggests a state-run process. The market is probably only hundreds of wells, with no licensed-well count found. Annual renewal is a real duty, but the niche is small and the buyers are fragmented.
